name: Abby Miller
summary: A schoolgirl whose death was prophesied by the Kimagure scroll. Her mother enlists Elektra to protect her from the Hand's assassin, Typhoid Mary.
source_notes: Played by Kirby Bliss Blanton in Elektra (2005).

name: Abigail Whistler
summary: Abraham Whistler's fiery daughter and the leader of the Nightstalkers, a band of vampire hunters. She helps Blade take down Dracula.
source_notes: Played by Jessica Biel in Blade: Trinity (2004).

name: Abraham Whistler
summary: Blade's gruff mentor who tracked down and trained the Daywalker, building the weaponry that lets Blade fight vampires. He aids Blade in the final stand against Dracula.
source_notes: Played by Kris Kristofferson in Blade (1998) and Blade: Trinity (2004).

name: Adam Warlock
summary: A bioengineered being nurtured by the Sovereign as a weapon against the Guardians. Born seemingly fully formed but childlike, he becomes a reluctant ally and joins the new Guardians, protecting the children of Knowhere.
source_notes: Featured prominently in the anti-credit scene of Vol. 2 and fully in Vol. 3.

name: AIDA
summary: An advanced artificial intelligence created by Holden Radcliffe, initially as a Life Model Decoy. She reads the Darkhold, becomes Madame HYDRA in the Framework, builds herself an Inhuman body, and is finally destroyed by Ghost Rider after declaring herself alive and turning on her creator.
image_alt: Promotional image released for the television show Agents of S.H.I.E.L.D. (2017). Featuring Mallory Jansen as Madame Hydra.
source_notes: Primary antagonist of Agents of S.H.I.E.L.D. season 4; plays three roles: the android AIDA, Madame HYDRA in the Framework, and the Inhuman host body.

name: Ajak
summary: The wise leader of the Eternals who could heal with cosmic energy and converse with the Celestials. She risked defying her mission and was killed by the Deviant Kro.
source_notes: Killed by Kro in Eternals (2021).

name: Alexandra Reid
summary: The reclusive, haughty leader of the Hand who for centuries sought the resurrection substance beneath New York. She was betrayed, stabbed and replaced by the newly-resurrected Elektra.
source_notes: Primary antagonist of The Defenders.

name: Alicia Masters
summary: A blind sculptor who is Ben Grimm's love interest. She sees past his rocky exterior and supports the team.
source_notes: Played by Kerry Washington in the 2005 films.
related_titles: Fantastic Four: Rise of the Silver Surfer (2007)

name: Alifah Halen
summary: A high-ranking member of the 'Real S.H.I.E.L.D.' who serves on the father of the faction alongside Robert Gonzalez. She is pragmatic and later accepts Coulson's leadership.
source_notes: Recurring in Agents of S.H.I.E.L.D. season 2.

name: Alphonso Mackenzie
summary: A former S.H.I.E.L.D. mechanic who becomes the team's heart, wielding his signature shotgun-axe. He leads the Resistance against the Framework's HYDRA regime, becomes Director of S.H.I.E.L.D. after the Chronicom war, and rebuilds the organisation in the epilogue.
source_notes: Recurring in season 2; series regular seasons 3–7 of Agents of S.H.I.E.L.D.

name: America Chavez
debut_title: Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness (2022)
summary: A young hero from another universe with the power to punch star-shaped portals through reality. She teams with Strange to stop Wanda and begins training at Kamar-Taj.
source_notes: Introduced in Multiverse of Madness (2022); trained by Strange and Wong.
related_titles: Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness (2022)

name: The Ancient One
summary: The centuries-old Sorcerer Supreme who protected Earth from dimensional threats. She denied Strange the Time Stone, then died defending Kamar-Taj, but appeared again during the Time Heist in Endgame.
source_notes: Killed by Kaecilius in Doctor Strange; meets Hulk/Banner during the Endgame Time Heist.

name: Anne Weying
summary: Eddie Brock's ex-fiancée and close friend, a lawyer who briefly bonded with the Venom symbiote to save a hostage and who continues to defend Eddie through the symbiote saga.
image_alt: Interior artwork from The Amazing Spider-Man vol. 1, 375 (March 1993 Marvel Comics) Art by Mark Magley
source_notes: Bonds with the symbiote to fight in Venom (2018).

name: Anya Corazon
summary: A whip-smart and determined Brooklyn teen, one of the three future spider-heroes protected by Cassandra Webb as they awake to their powers.
source_notes: Adaptation of Anya Corazon, the comics' Spider-Girl.

name: En Sabah Nur
summary: The world's first mutant, an ancient godlike being who amasses power and recruits four Horsemen to remake the world. He is the antagonist of X-Men: Apocalypse.
source_notes: Played by Oscar Isaac in X-Men: Apocalypse (2016).

name: Attuma
summary: The fierce Talokanil war chief who leads the underwater kingdom's assaults against Wakanda.
source_notes: A secondary antagonist of Wakanda Forever.

name: May Parker
summary: Peter's warm, principled aunt who raised him after his parents died and nearly died of illness until Peter used his power to save her. She married again and survived into the No Way Home era.
source_notes: A stabilizing moral influence on Peter across the trilogy.

name: May Parker
summary: The sharp-tongued but loving aunt who raised Peter with her late husband Ben, eventually learning and accepting that Peter is Spider-Man.
source_notes: A more independent, knowing Aunt May than the Raimi version.

name: Ayo
summary: A senior Dora Milaje warrior who became leader of the Dora Milaje in Wakanda Forever after Okoye's dismissal.
source_notes: Florence Kasumba's recurring Dora Milaje warrior.

name: Baron Wolfgang von Strucker
summary: The ruthless leader of HYDRA who plots to destroy the eastern seaboard's telecommunications with a super-weapon. He is killed by Nick Fury.
source_notes: Played by Neil Roberts in the 1998 television film, a distinct variant from Thomas Kretschmann's MCU Baron Strucker.

name: Hank McCoy
debut_title: X-Men: The Last Stand (2006; Fox continuity)
summary: The blue-furred genius
source_notes: Confirmed for Avengers: Doomsday (cross-listed from the 30-member cast)

name: Hank McCoy
summary: A brilliant scientist and mutant with superhuman agility and a blue-furred appearance. A key member and thinker among the X-Men in both timelines, and a Cabinet-secretary rebel in Days of Future Past.
source_notes: Played by Kelsey Grammer and Nicholas Hoult.

name: Ben Grimm
summary: The Thing
source_notes: Confirmed for Avengers: Doomsday (cross-listed from the 30-member cast)

name: Ben Grimm
summary: A kind-hearted pilot transformed into a rocky, super-strong orange brute by cosmic radiation. He struggles with his appearance but remains the team's fearless powerhouse and Reed's best friend.
source_notes: Played by Michael Chiklis (2005, practical suit) and Jamie Bell (2015, CGI).
related_titles: Fantastic Four: Rise of the Silver Surfer (2007)

name: Benjamin Poindexter
summary: A psychopathic FBI agent with impossibly precise aim who is manipulated by Kingpin into wearing a Daredevil suit and terrorizing Hell's Kitchen. He was rendered crippled but surgically repaired to become Bullseye.
source_notes: Teased as Bullseye in the season 3 finale; returns in Daredevil: Born Again.

name: Beverly Switzler
summary: A struggling rock singer who befriends and becomes the romantic partner of the stranded Howard the Duck, helping him battle the dark overlord.
source_notes: Played by Lea Thompson in Howard the Duck (1986).

name: Billy Russo
summary: Frank Castle's former best friend and black-ops colleague turned enemy, a mercenary who killed Frank's family. The punishing confrontation left his face disfigured into the living puzzle of Jigsaw.
source_notes: Scarred and remade as Jigsaw across The Punisher's two seasons.

name: Natasha Romanoff
summary: Former S.H.I.E.L.D. spy and assassin who defected to the Avengers. Natasha sacrificed herself on Vormir in 2023 so her family could have the Soul Stone.
source_notes: Original six founding Avenger; died on Vormir in Endgame (2019).

name: Blackheart
summary: The rebellious son of the Devil who attempts to steal a contract with 1,000 souls to overthrow his father. He is dragged screaming into Hell by the Ghost Rider's Penance Stare.
source_notes: Primary antagonist of Ghost Rider (2007).

name: Eric Brooks
summary: A half-vampire, half-human hybrid who hunts vampires. Loyal only to his mentor Whistler and his network of allies, he fights against a vampire conspiracy to awaken the ancient vampire lord Dracula.
source_notes: Played by Wesley Snipes in the Blade trilogy (1998–2004). The character is slated to join the MCU, played by Mahershala Ali, in the upcoming Blade.

name: Bucky Barnes
summary: The Winter Soldier
image_alt: Promotional image of Sebastian Stan as Bucky Barnes in the Marvel Studios film, Captain America: The Winter Soldier.
source_notes: Confirmed for Avengers: Doomsday (cross-listed from the 30-member cast)
related_titles: The Falcon and the Winter Soldier (2021)

name: Bullseye
summary: A bald, psychopathic assassin who can turn virtually anything into a lethal projectile. He kills Elektra and is in turn killed by Daredevil.
source_notes: Played by Colin Farrell in Daredevil (2003), a distinct variant from the Netflix Bullseye.

name: Nathan Summers
summary: A grizzled, cybernetic mutant soldier from a dystopian future who travels back in time to prevent a tragedy, reluctantly teaming with Deadpool.
source_notes: Played by Josh Brolin in Deadpool 2 (2018).

name: Calypso Ezili
summary: A forensic psychiatrist who aids Sergei Kravinoff and is drawn into his violent family affairs, serving as his confidante.
source_notes: Comic counterpart is the voodoo priestess Calypso.

name: Steve Rogers
summary: A weak young man transformed by the Super-Soldier Serum into Captain America. Frozen during World War II, he is revived in the 1990s to stop the Red Skull's catastrophic plot.
source_notes: Played by Matt Salinger in Captain America (1990), the final pre-MCU Captain America film.

name: Steve Rogers
summary: The Sentinel of Liberty
source_notes: Confirmed for Avengers: Doomsday (cross-listed from the 30-member cast)

name: Cletus Kasady
summary: A serial killer and Eddie's estranged childhood acquaintance who bonded with the offspring of the Venom symbiote, becoming the sadistic red monster Carnage. He was destroyed alongside his symbiote.
source_notes: Primary antagonist of Venom: Let There Be Carnage.

name: Carol Danvers
summary: A U.S. Air Force pilot who gained cosmic powers after an explosion exposed her to the Tesseract's energy. One of the MCU's most powerful heroes, she answers Nick Fury's pager in Endgame and later balances Earth defense with intergalactic responsibility.
source_notes: Central to The Marvels (2023) with Monica Rambeau and Kamala Khan.

name: Carter Slade
summary: The previous Ghost Rider who now serves as a caretaker and mentor to Johnny Blaze, offering guidance on how to wield the Rider's power.
source_notes: Played by Sam Elliott in Ghost Rider (2007).

name: Cassie Lang
summary: The size-shifting Stature
image_alt: Kathryn Newton during an interview for Ant-Man and The Wasp: Quantamania in February 2023
source_notes: Confirmed for Avengers: Doomsday (cross-listed from the 30-member cast)

name: Charles Xavier
summary: The telepathic founder and leader of the X-Men who dreams of peaceful mutant-human coexistence. In the 2024 film Deadpool & Wolverine he abdicated his Earth-10005 Xavier's School responsibilities to the X-Men at large.
source_notes: Played by Patrick Stewart in the original timeline and James McAvoy in the young-timeline prequels; appears in Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness (2022).

name: Christine Palmer
summary: A trauma surgeon and Stephen Strange's former colleague and ex-girlfriend. She attended his wedding in an alternate universe in Multiverse of Madness.
source_notes: Appears in Doctor Strange and Multiverse of Madness.
related_titles: Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness (2022)

name: Claire Temple
summary: An ER nurse who repeatedly patches up street-level heroes across every Netflix Marvel series, becoming the connective tissue who knows Daredevil, Jessica, Luke, Danny and Frank by their real names.
source_notes: Appears in Daredevil, Jessica Jones, Luke Cage and Iron Fist.

name: Clea
debut_title: Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness (2022)
summary: A sorceress from the Dark Dimension, daughter of Dormammu in the comics, who recruits Strange to help fix an incursion in the post-credits scene of Multiverse of Madness.
source_notes: Set up as Strange's next ally in Multiverse of Madness's post-credits scene.
related_titles: Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness (2022)

name: Colleen Wing
summary: A US-Japanese martial-arts teacher running Chikara Dojo, Danny Rand's ally and eventual partner. She inherits the iron fist after Danny renounces it, reclaiming her family's lost weapon.
source_notes: Revealed as the rightful bearer of the iron fist in season 2.

name: Piotr Rasputin
summary: A gentle Russian mutant who can transform his body into organic steel, giving him superhuman strength and durability. He serves as Deadpool's exasperated moral compass.
source_notes: Voiced by Stefan Kapičić in the Deadpool films.

name: Cornell Stokes
summary: The slick owner of Harlem's Paradise who ran the neighbourhood's crime while dreaming of restoring its power and pride. He was murdered by his own cousin Mariah Dillard.
source_notes: Season 1's first major antagonist of Luke Cage.

name: Curtis Hoyle
summary: Frank Castle's one-legged war buddy who runs a veterans' support group, the moral conscience who keeps trying to pull Frank back from the abyss of total revenge.
source_notes: Frank's most loyal friend and anchor.

name: Scott Summers
summary: The optic-blast field commander
source_notes: Confirmed for Avengers: Doomsday (cross-listed from the 30-member cast)

name: Scott Summers
summary: The disciplined field leader of the X-Men whose eyes emit powerful energy beams he controls with a visor. He is Jean Grey's longtime partner.
source_notes: Played by James Marsden and Tye Sheridan.

name: Daisy Johnson
summary: A gifted S.H.I.E.L.D. agent and Inhuman with seismic powers who begins as a hacker named Skye. After undergoing Terrigenesis she becomes Quake, leads the Secret Warriors, and eventually takes over as field director of S.H.I.E.L.D.
source_notes: Co-lead of Agents of S.H.I.E.L.D. seasons 1–7; Skye's real name revealed as Daisy Johnson in season 2.

name: Eli Damaskinos
summary: The shadowy Pureblood leader of the Prague vampire council who engineered the Reaper experiment. He attempts to use Blade to end the Reaper threat, then betrays him.
source_notes: Primary antagonist of the first half of Blade II (2002).

name: Danica Talos
summary: The ruthless acting head of the vampire nation who hunts Blade and the Nightstalkers. She is killed by Abigail Whistler.
source_notes: Primary villain of the first act of Blade: Trinity (2004).

name: Daniel Sousa
summary: A World War II veteran and original S.S.R. agent who is recruited by S.H.I.E.L.D. in 1946 and later pulled forward in time by the Chronicom war. He becomes a key member of Coulson's team and establishes the framework for the modern S.H.I.E.L.D.
source_notes: Recurring in Agent Carter season 2; regular in Agents of S.H.I.E.L.D. season 7. Enver Gjokaj also played a Chitauri-soldier cameo in The Avengers (2012).

name: Danny Rand
summary: The last survivor of a plane crash, raised in the mystical city of K'un-Lun and granted the iron fist after defeating the dragon Shou-Lao. He returns to New York to reclaim Rand Enterprises, fights the Hand, and eventually renounces the iron fist to end their war.
source_notes: The comics' storm-summoning marks him as a potential avatar of Shou-Lao.

name: Darcy Lewis
summary: A political science student turned doctor who assists Jane Foster across the Thor films, later interned with S.W.O.R.D. and helped analyze Wanda's hex in WandaVision.
source_notes: Appears in WandaVision (2021) as a S.W.O.R.D. scientist.

name: Darren Cross
summary: Hank Pym's estranged protégé who weaponized shrinking tech as the Yellowjacket. He was defeated and shrunk to sub-atomic size by Scott Lang.
source_notes: A variant of Darren Cross appears as MODOK in Quantumania (2023).

name: David Darrows
summary: A loyal S.H.I.E.L.D. agent who serves on Coulson's team during the HYDRA uprising and beyond. He is one of the agents killed during the Battle at the Hub but is later referenced in the Framework.
source_notes: Recurring in Agents of S.H.I.E.L.D. seasons 1–2; Maximiliano Hernández also played Jasper Sitwell in the MCU films.

name: Davos
summary: Danny Rand's foster brother from K'un-Lun who was denied the iron fist. Bitter and ruthless, he steals the power and becomes the Steel Serpent of legend, fighting Colleen Wing for the mantle.
source_notes: Season 2's primary antagonist.

name: Deacon Frost
summary: An ambitious, contemptuous vampire who seeks to overthrow the vampire hierarchy and summon the Blood God La Magra. He is killed by Blade.
source_notes: Primary antagonist of Blade (1998).

name: Wade Wilson
summary: A wisecracking, fourth-wall-breaking mercenary with a powerful healing factor. His meta, R-rated solo films became Fox's biggest Marvel successes, and he joins the MCU's wider multiverse alongside Wolverine in 2024.
source_notes: Played by Ryan Reynolds; Deadpool & Wolverine (2024) is technically MCU-set but follows his Fox-era continuity.
notes: Appears in the upcoming Avengers: Doomsday (2026).

name: Willis Stryker
summary: Luke Cage's foster brother turned arms dealer, a fanatical Christ-complex villain who wore armour-piercing Judas bullets and targeted everyone Luke loved. He died grasping at Luke's waist while both fell.
source_notes: Season 1's ultimate antagonist.

name: Dinah Madani
summary: A dogged DHS special agent hunting the A-plot conspiracy around Frank Castle's family. She allies with Frank without approving his methods, shutting down the agency's corrupt scheme over two seasons.
source_notes: Frank's uneasy government ally.

name: Victor von Doom
summary: The Multiverse Saga threat
source_notes: Confirmed for Avengers: Doomsday (cross-listed from the 30-member cast)

name: Victor Von Doom
summary: A brilliant but arrogant scientist whose rivalry with Reed Richards turns to villainy. In the films he gains metal-based powers that twist him into a despot bent on conquering Earth.
image_alt: Nu riff di funeral doom di circa 30 sicunni.
source_notes: Played by Julian McMahon (2005) and Toby Kebbell (2015). The character is slated to appear as the central antagonist of Avengers: Doomsday (2026).
related_titles: Fantastic Four: Rise of the Silver Surfer (2007)
notes: Reimagined as the central antagonist of the upcoming Avengers: Doomsday (2026), played by Robert Downey Jr.

name: Otto Octavius
summary: A brilliant physicist whose fusion experiment fused four mechanical tentacles to his spine and corrupted his mind. He drowned saving the city, but a pre-corruption variant was pulled into the MCU in No Way Home.
source_notes: Redemptive antagonist of Spider-Man 2 (2004); variant appears in No Way Home.

name: Stephen Strange
summary: A brilliant neurosurgeon who became Sorcerer Supreme's defender of reality after a car accident destroyed his hands. He wielded the Time Stone to bargain for half the universe, only for the Snap to still happen, and now guards the Multiverse.
source_notes: Wielded the Time Stone; central to Infinity War through Multiverse of Madness.
related_titles: Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness (2022)

name: Neena Thurman
summary: A mutant whose power is improbably good luck, bending probability in her favor. She joins Deadpool's X-Force and proves invaluable in Deadpool 2.
source_notes: Played by Zazie Beetz in Deadpool 2 (2018).

name: Dormammu
summary: The all-consuming ruler of the Dark Dimension who hungers to absorb realities. Doctor Strange trapped him in an endless time loop until he relented.
source_notes: Voiced by Benedict Cumberbatch; defeated by a time loop in Doctor Strange.

name: Dracula
summary: The original vampire sire and patriarch of the entire vampire race, resurrected from a mummified state to lead the vampire nation. Defeated when Blade infects him with a vampire-wolf serum and feeds on his blood.
source_notes: Primary antagonist of Blade: Trinity (2004).

name: Drax
summary: A grieving warrior whose family was murdered by Ronan. He joins the Guardians seeking vengeance, and over time softens into a comic-relief father figure before joining the team's new era and eventually staying on Knowhere to raise the children.
source_notes: Stays on Knowhere with Nebula at the end of Vol. 3 rather than departing with the new team.

name: Druig
summary: An Eternal with telepathic and telekinetic abilities to control minds. He broke away to live in isolation, then rejoined his family to save Earth.
source_notes: Romantically paired with Makkari.

name: Eddie Brock
summary: A rival photographer who bonded with the black alien symbiote that had briefly corrupted Spider-Man. The union created the monstrous Venom, who teamed with Sandman before being destroyed along with the symbiote.
source_notes: The Raimi-universe Venom, separate from the Tom Hardy version.

name: Ego
summary: An ancient Celestial who is himself a living planet and the biological father of Peter Quill. He planned to terraform the universe in his image using Peter's power, and was destroyed by the Guardians in 2014.
source_notes: Ego's death in Vol. 2 is the reason Peter loses his Celestial powers.

name: Max Dillon
summary: An overlooked Oscorp electrical engineer who transformed into a being of pure electrical power after an accident, resenting the world and Spider-Man. A variant returned energy-starved in No Way Home.
source_notes: Appears in No Way Home, seeking the Arc Reactor.

name: Elektra Natchios
summary: A deadly assassin who romances Matt Murdock. Believed killed by Bullseye, she returns in her own spinoff film, fighting for a young girl threatened by the Hand and their super-powered foes.
source_notes: Played by Jennifer Garner in Daredevil (2003) and Elektra (2005).

name: Elektra Natchios
summary: A deadly assassin trained by Stick who shares a volatile love with Matt Murdock. Killed by Nobu, she was resurrected by the substance of the Hand, becoming the Black Sky before sacrificing herself to collapse Midland Circle.
source_notes: Loved-and-lost figure across Daredevil and The Defenders.

name: Ellie Halbeck
summary: A senior S.H.I.E.L.D. officer stationed at The Hub who oversees field operations. He provides missions and intelligence to Coulson's team during the pre-HYDRA era.
source_notes: Recurring in Agents of S.H.I.E.L.D. season 1.

name: Erik Stevens
summary: A Wakandan-American black ops soldier who sought to use Wakanda's weapons to liberate oppressed peoples worldwide. He defeated T'Challa for the throne before being fatally wounded, choosing death over capture.
source_notes: The acclaimed antagonist of Black Panther (2018).

name: Erik Selvig
summary: An astrophysicist who aided Thor on Midgard, was manipulated by Loki into launching the Chitauri invasion, and later helped analyze the Convergence in The Dark World.
image_alt: Promotional image released for the television show Thor (2011). Featuring Stellan Skarsgård as Erik Selvig.
source_notes: Manipulated by Loki via the Mind Stone in The Avengers (2012).

name: Everett K. Ross
summary: A CIA deputy task force commander who partners with Wakanda across films, later arrested and rescued by Everett and Okoye in Wakanda Forever.
source_notes: Appears in Civil War, Black Panther, Infinity War, and Wakanda Forever.

name: Ezekiel Sims
summary: A wealthy industrialist who gained spider powers in the Peruvian Amazon and used his future-visions to hunt down the young women destined to become the Spider-Women before they can appear.
source_notes: Antagonist of Madame Web; spider-powers mirroring the Spider-People.

name: Fandral
summary: A dashing swordsman of the Warriors Three who fights for Asgard until Hela kills him in Thor: Ragnarok.
source_notes: Originally played by Joshua Dallas in Thor (2011); recast with Zachary Levi from The Dark World onward.

name: Leopold Fitz / Jemma Simmons
summary: S.H.I.E.L.D.'s brilliant scientific duo: Fitz is an engineering genius and Simmons a biochemist. Separated by space, time, and alternate timelines, they persistently find each other. Their LMD and Chronicom-based tech saves the team in the final war.
source_notes: Co-lead characters in Agents of S.H.I.E.L.D. seasons 1–7; often referred to as a single unit by the team.

name: Floor
summary: A three-legged white hare and one of Rocket's lab-mates in the High Evolutionary's experiments. She was working on escaping her enclosure when the team's escape was betrayed, and she was killed in the crossfire.
source_notes: Vol. 3 flashback character.

name: Franklin Nelson
summary: Matt's law partner and loyal best friend, the pragmatic heart of Nelson & Murdock. He repeatedly solves cases through dogged legal work while wrestling with Matt's dual identity.
image_alt: Fred Nelson III and Aretha Franklin
source_notes: Comedic relief and moral counterweight to Matt.

name: Franklin Nelson
summary: Matt Murdock's best friend and law partner. He is the warm, comic-relief conscience of the pair.
source_notes: Played by Jon Favreau in Daredevil (2003).

name: Unknown / The Foreigner
summary: A lethal assassin hired to kill a Mobster whom Kraven protects. His fatal encounter with one of Kraven's animal allies sets off the film's violent chain of events.
image_alt: King Abdulaziz with a Foreigner in the 1930s
source_notes: Classic Spider-Man mercenary adapted for the SSU.

name: Frank Castle
summary: A former FBI agent turned vigilante who wages a one-man war against crime after his family is murdered by the Saint family. He targets Howard Saint with ruthless precision.
source_notes: Played by Thomas Jane in The Punisher (2004), a distinct variant from the Netflix and War Zone versions.

name: Frank Castle
summary: A decorated Marine whose family was executed under a conspiracy he later joined the military's censorship. He wages a ruthless one-man war on criminals, at war with his own methods alongside Daredevil, and returned as a covert dealer of justice.
source_notes: Debuts in Daredevil season 2; returns in Daredevil: Born Again (2025).

name: Frank Castle
summary: A brutal vigilante who wages war against New York's organized crime. His battle with the disfigured Jigsaw escalates until he destroys the mob and its corrupt officials.
source_notes: Played by Ray Stevenson in Punisher: War Zone (2008), a distinct variant from the 2004 film.

name: Franklin Storm
summary: The senior scientist whose experiments in the 2015 reboot accidentally trigger the accident that gives the Four their powers.
source_notes: Played by Andre Braugher in Fantastic Four (2015).

name: Frigga
summary: Odin's wife and mother to Thor and Loki, whom she loved as her own. She taught Loki magic and sorcery, and was killed by Malekith's forces in Thor: The Dark World. Thor reunites with her during his Time Heist in Endgame.
image_alt: Promotional image of Rene Russo as Frigga in the Marvel Studios film, Thor.
source_notes: Killed in The Dark World (2013); appears to the past-Thor in Endgame's Time Heist.

name: Gable Hoover
summary: A S.H.I.E.L.D. academy student who is among the few survivors of the Framework Collapse and joins the Resistance. He is loyal to May and serves as a reliable operative during the Chronicom war.
source_notes: Minor recurring character in Agents of S.H.I.E.L.D. seasons 4–7.

name: Galactus
debut_title: Fantastic Four: Rise of the Silver Surfer (2007)
summary: An ancient cosmic entity that consumes planets to sustain itself. He serves as the apocalyptic threat in Rise of the Silver Surfer, depicted as a planet-devouring storm cloud in the 2007 film.
source_notes: Voiced by Laurence Fishburne in Fantastic Four: Rise of the Silver Surfer (2007).
related_titles: Fantastic Four: Rise of the Silver Surfer (2007)

name: Remy LeBeau
summary: The ragin Cajun
source_notes: Confirmed for Avengers: Doomsday (cross-listed from the 30-member cast)

name: Remy LeBeau
summary: A Cajun thief and mutant who charges objects with kinetic energy and throws explosive playing cards. He appears briefly in Wolverine's origin film and returns in Deadpool & Wolverine (2024).
source_notes: Played by Taylor Kitsch (2009) and Channing Tatum (Deadpool & Wolverine 2024).

name: Gamora
aliases: The Deadliest Woman in the Galaxy
summary: The last daughter of Thanos, trained as an assassin before defecting to the Guardians. Thanos sacrificed her on Vormir for the Soul Stone in 2018. A 2014-era variant displaced into the present during Endgame survives and finds a new home with the Ravagers.
source_notes: Original timeline Gamora dies on Vormir (Infinity War); a 2014 variant survives Endgame and Vol. 3.
notes: Separate record from the surviving 2014 variant is not kept; the current MCU Gamora is that variant.

name: George Stacy
summary: Gwen's protective father and an NYPD captain who investigated Spider-Man, learning his identity only after being fatally wounded saving him from the Lizard. He made Peter promise to stay away from Gwen.
source_notes: His dying request sets up the tragedy with Gwen.

name: Ava Starr
summary: The phasing Ghost
image_alt: Alex Montiel entrevistando a Hannah John-Kamen y a Jake Schreier en la Comic-Con de San Diego 2024
source_notes: Confirmed for Avengers: Doomsday (cross-listed from the 30-member cast)

name: Robbie Reyes
summary: A Los Angeles car enthusiast who is resurrected by the Spirit of Vengeance after being murdered by his uncle. He wields a flaming Dodge Charger and hellfire chain, briefly works with S.H.I.E.L.D. to contain the Darkhold's effects, and is pulled through a portal to an alternate Earth.
source_notes: Recurring in Agents of S.H.I.E.L.D. season 4; Gabriel Luna was announced for a Ghost Rider Disney+ series that was ultimately shelved.

name: Gideon Malick
summary: The secret head of HYDRA's ancient council who uses the portal to Maveth to summon the Inhuman known as Hive. He betrays Ward and aligns with the parasitic monster, but is killed when Hive is destroyed.
source_notes: Recurring antagonist in Agents of S.H.I.E.L.D. seasons 2–3; also appeared in The Avengers (2012) as a World Security Council member.

name: Gilgamesh
summary: A powerful Eternal who forged cosmic-energy weapons and armor, and the devoted caretaker of Thena. He was killed by the Deviant Kro while protecting her.
source_notes: Killed by Kro in Eternals (2021).

name: Gorr
summary: A grieving father who swore to kill all gods after his prayers went unanswered, wielding the necrosword to strike across the universe. He is undone in part by Thor's empathy and wished back his daughter at his end.
source_notes: The primary antagonist of Love and Thunder (2022).

name: Grandmaster
summary: The flamboyant ruler of Sakaar who runs its gladiator games. Deposed by the revolution he himself inspired, he is last seen (in an apparent earlier timeline) at a casino on Knowhere.
source_notes: Cameo in the Knowhere post-credits scene of Thor 3's predecessor adjacent material.

name: Grant Ward
summary: A S.H.I.E.L.D. trainee who is secretly a HYDRA sleeper agent raised by John Garrett. His betrayal collapses the team, and he rises to become the new face of HYDRA after being stranded on Maveth. He is killed by Daisy but later inhabits a Framework copy and an LMD body before finally being destroyed.
source_notes: Main antagonist of Agents of S.H.I.E.L.D. seasons 1–4; Brett Dalton also plays the Framework version and an LMD copy.

name: Norman Osborn
summary: The brilliant, ruthless founder of Oscorp who split into a murderous Green Goblin persona after his experimental serum. He died at his own glider in 2002, but a variant crossed over in No Way Home and fatally wounded Aunt May.
source_notes: Killed by his own glider in Spider-Man (2002); returns as a variant in No Way Home.

name: Harry Osborn
summary: The embittered son of Norman Osborn who blamed Peter for his father's death. He experimented on himself, becoming the Goblin and killing Gwen Stacy before dying of his injuries.
source_notes: Responsible for Gwen Stacy's death.

name: Groot
summary: A tree-like Flora Colossus who sacrifices himself to save his family in the first film, regrown from a twig as Baby Groot. The current Groot, now a full adult in Vol. 3, enters a new unlikely partnership with Rocket.
source_notes: Original Groot dies in Guardians 1; the twig Groot is a distinct growth of the same character and featured in the I Am Groot shorts.

name: Gwen Stacy
summary: A scientist's daughter and a brief love rival to Mary Jane in Spider-Man 3, whom Venom targeted to hurt Spider-Man.
source_notes: Minor role in Spider-Man 3; distinct from the Webb-universe Gwen.

name: Gwen Stacy
summary: A brilliant Oscorp scientist and Peter's girlfriend, whose death - snapped by the Green Goblin - became the defining tragedy of the Webb films and Peter's deepest regret.
source_notes: Her death in The Amazing Spider-Man 2 haunts the Garfield version.

name: Hank Pym
summary: The brilliant inventor of the Pym Particles that allow shrinking and growing. A founding member of the Avengers in the comics, in the MCU he was a S.H.I.E.L.D. scientist who retired and later trained Scott Lang.
source_notes: Founding Avenger in Marvel comics; in the MCU he is retired when Scott Lang takes the mantle.

name: Hannibal King
summary: A wisecracking vampire private eye who joins the Nightstalkers against Dracula. He is later cured by the blood of a vampire-wolf hybrid.
source_notes: Played by Ryan Reynolds in Blade: Trinity (2004).

name: Harold Meachum
summary: The corrupt CEO of Rand Enterprises who abandoned Danny as a child and secretly served the Hand. Repeatedly resurrected after his apparent deaths, he was finally killed for good by Ward.
source_notes: Season 1's principal antagonist.

name: Harry Osborn
summary: Peter's best friend and Norman Osborn's son, who inherited the Goblin mantle believing Spider-Man killed his father. He discovered Peter's identity, saved him from Venom, and died from his injuries after reconciling.
source_notes: Becomes the New Goblin in Spider-Man 3 (2007).

name: Clint Barton
summary: Master archer and the grounded heart of the Avengers. During the Blip he operated as the masked vigilante Ronin before the Time Heist and reunion with his family.
source_notes: Debuts via cameo in Thor (2011); original-six Avenger.

name: Heimdall
summary: The all-seeing gatekeeper of the Bifrost and protector of Asgard. He smuggled the New Asgardians aboard the Statesman and was killed by Thanos in the cold open of Avengers: Infinity War.
image_alt: Promotional image of Idris Elba as Heimdall in the Marvel Studios film, Thor.
source_notes: Killed by Thanos in Infinity War (2018) before Thor arrives.

name: Hela
summary: Odin's firstborn, the Goddess of Death, imprisoned for millennia for her conquest. Freed by Odin's death, she destroyed Asgard's armies and the Warriors Three before Surtur destroyed Asgard with her on it.
source_notes: Defeated when Surtur destroys Asgard in Ragnarok; her fate with the planet is implied death.

name: High Evolutionary
summary: A brilliant but brutally narcissistic geneticist who created Rocket and an entire civilization on Counter-Earth. The Guardians defeat him, and he is left stranded and disfigured on his ruined flagship.
source_notes: Creator of Rocket; the primary antagonist of Vol. 3.

name: Hive
summary: An ancient Inhuman parasitic entity who founded HYDRA millennia ago and was banished to Maveth. He inhabits Ward's corpse after returning to Earth and attempts to transform all humans into Inhumans using a Kree rock. He is destroyed when a centrifuge fires him into a Zephyr One engine.
source_notes: Primary antagonist of Agents of S.H.I.E.L.D. season 3; Brett Dalton plays both Ward and Hive.

name: Hogun
summary: A stoic Asgardian warrior of the Warriors Three, the last to fall when Hela slaughters them in Thor: Ragnarok.
source_notes: Killed by Hela in Ragnarok (2017).

name: Holden Radcliffe
summary: A transhumanist bioethicist who builds the artificial intelligence A.I.D.A. and becomes obsessed with immortality through the Darkhold. He creates the Framework as a virtual paradise but loses control of his creation, eventually being killed by the Russian Ghost Rider.
source_notes: Antagonist of Agents of S.H.I.E.L.D. season 4; John Hannah's second MCU role after a 2005 Marvel film.

name: Hope van Dyne
summary: Hank and Janet's daughter who takes up the Wasp mantle and fights alongside Scott Lang. She joins the Avengers and participates in the Battle of Earth.
source_notes: Active Avenger in Endgame's final battle.

name: Howard Saint
summary: A wealthy Tampa crime lord who orders the murder of Frank Castle's family in retaliation, setting off the Punisher's campaign of vengeance. He is destroyed alongside his entire organization.
source_notes: Primary antagonist of The Punisher (2004).

name: Howard Stark
summary: Tony Stark's brilliant father and a founder of S.H.I.E.L.D. He worked on the Tesseract and the super-soldier project, and was murdered by the Winter Soldier in 1991.
source_notes: Played by John Slattery as an adult; murdered by Bucky under Hydra control in 1991.

name: Howard
summary: A wisecracking, anthropomorphic duck from the planet Duckworld who is accidentally dragged to Earth by a laser experiment. He battles an interdimensional evil overlord and saves Earth, later appearing in the MCU's post-credits scenes.
source_notes: Played by Ed Gale (suit) with Chip Zien's voice in Howard the Duck (1986). An MCU variant voiced by Seth Green appears in Guardians of the Galaxy and Avengers: Endgame.

name: Bruce Banner
summary: Gamma-radiated physicist who fused his mind with the Hulk as Professor Hulk. Held the gauntlet through the final battle of Endgame and now studies gamma radiation with his cousin.
source_notes: Single-cast origins: Edward Norton in The Incredible Hulk (2008) as separate continuity of the role; Mark Ruffalo assumed the part from The Avengers (2012).

name: Bobby Drake
summary: A young mutant who can freeze moisture and form ice, and one of the earliest X-Men students. His coming-out as a mutant to his family is a defining scene in X-Men 2.
source_notes: Played by Shawn Ashmore.

name: Ikaris
summary: The most powerful Eternal, able to fly and project cosmic energy. Torn between his love for Sersi and his duty to the Celestials, he chooses to fly into the sun after failing to stop the Emergence.
source_notes: Flies into the sun at the end of Eternals (2021).

name: Tony Stark
summary: Billionaire genius, philanthropist and founding Avenger who built the first functional Iron Man suit in a cave from scraps. Tony used the Infinity Stones in 2023 to undo the Snap and died of their power in the Battle of Earth.
source_notes: Founding Avenger of the original six; deceased in Endgame (2019). Downey is separately confirmed as Doctor Doom in Avengers: Doomsday — a distinct character record (doctor-doom).
notes: Record kept distinct from doctor-doom; both are played by Robert Downey Jr.

name: Jack Murdock
summary: Matt's father, a washed-up boxer who refused to throw a fight and was murdered on the Kingpin's orders, triggering Matt's quest for justice.
source_notes: Played by David Keith in Daredevil (2003).

name: Jane Foster
summary: An astrophysicist and Thor's former love who bonded to the shattered Mjolnir in Thor: Love and Thunder, becoming the Mighty Thor as she battled cancer.
image_alt: Promotional image of Chris Hemsworth as Thor and Natalie Portman as Jane Foster in the Marvel Studios film, Thor.
source_notes: Becomes Mighty Thor in Love and Thunder (2022) and dies of her illness in the film.

name: Janet Van Dyne
summary: Hank Pym's wife and the original Wasp, who spent thirty years lost in the Quantum Realm and returned with a greater understanding of its power. She mentored her daughter Hope.
source_notes: Lost in the Quantum Realm from 1987 to 2018.

name: Jean Grey
summary: An immensely powerful telekinetic and telepath who hosts the cosmic Phoenix Force. Her destructive Dark Phoenix persona is a recurring tragedy across the Fox films, culminating in Dark Phoenix (2019).
source_notes: Played by Famke Janssen (adult) and Sophie Turner (young); the Phoenix arc adapts the classic comics storyline.

name: Jeri Hogarth
summary: The brilliant, ruthless high-power attorney who hired Jessica Jones and later became her legal ally, battling ALS and her own mortality while securing Jessica's freedom.
source_notes: The only lawyer Jessica trusts; facing ALS in the final season.

name: Jessica Jones
summary: A jaded private investigator with superhuman strength and a purple-victim's trauma. Bitter, alcoholic and fiercely independent, she repeatedly hunts her abuser Kilgrave and protects the powerless of Hell's Kitchen.
source_notes: Granted powers in a car accident that killed her family.

name: Billy Russo
summary: A vicious mobster disfigured by shattered glass in a fight with the Punisher, becoming the monster known as Jigsaw. He wages a brutal campaign of retaliation before being killed.
source_notes: Played by Dominic West in Punisher: War Zone (2008), a distinct variant from the Netflix Billy Russo.

name: Jimmy Woo
summary: A by-the-book FBI agent who supervised Scott Lang's house arrest and later investigated Wanda's Westview anomaly in WandaVision, where he became a fan-favorite magician-in-training.
source_notes: Featured in WandaVision (2021).

name: J. Jonah Jameson
summary: The blustery, anti-spider crusading editor of the Daily Bugle who pays Peter for photos of Spider-Man. The same J.K. Simmons incarnation later headlines the MCU's YouTube-style bugle in Far From Home.
source_notes: A variant played by J.K. Simmons appears in the MCU (Far From Home onward).

name: Joaquin Torres
debut_title: The Falcon and the Winter Soldier (2021)
summary: The new Falcon
source_notes: Confirmed for Avengers: Doomsday (cross-listed from the 30-member cast)
related_titles: The Falcon and the Winter Soldier (2021)

name: John Garrett
summary: A veteran S.H.I.E.L.D. agent and Ward's mentor who is secretly the HYDRA leader known as the Clairvoyant. He uses Project T.A.H.I.T.I. to cheat death but is ultimately killed by Coulson.
source_notes: Primary antagonist of Agents of S.H.I.E.L.D. season 1; Bill Paxton's final TV role.

name: John Walker
debut_title: The Falcon and the Winter Soldier (2021)
summary: U.S. Agent
image_alt: Chronophotograph at high speed. Johnnie Walker splash without any montage! Glass was glued to an inclined plane, which was dropped to create the splash
source_notes: Confirmed for Avengers: Doomsday (cross-listed from the 30-member cast)
related_titles: The Falcon and the Winter Soldier (2021)

name: Johnny Blaze
summary: A motorcycle stuntman who sells his soul to Mephistopheles to save his father, becoming the fiery Ghost Rider. He rides a flaming motorcycle and hunts the damned, later returning to defeat the Devil's son in Spirit of Vengeance.
source_notes: Played by Nicolas Cage in Ghost Rider (2007) and Ghost Rider: Spirit of Vengeance (2011).

name: Johnny Storm
summary: The Human Torch
image_alt: Artwork for the cover of Fantastic Four vol. 4, 645 (April 2015 Marvel Comics) Art by Michael Komarck (Variant cover art)
source_notes: Confirmed for Avengers: Doomsday (cross-listed from the 30-member cast)

name: Johnny Storm
summary: Sue's impulsive younger brother who can engulf himself in flame, fly, and throw fireballs. He is the team's cocky hothead and resident flirt.
source_notes: Played by Chris Evans (2005) and Michael B. Jordan (2015); a variant of Johnny Storm also appears in Deadpool & Wolverine (2024).
related_titles: Fantastic Four: Rise of the Silver Surfer (2007)

name: Cain Marko
summary: An unstoppable armored powerhouse, Charles Xavier's stepbrother, who rampages through his foes' ranks. He appears in The Last Stand and as a CGI prison-cell monster in Deadpool 2.
source_notes: Played by Vinnie Jones (2006) and voiced by Ryan Reynolds in Deadpool 2 (2018).

name: Julia Cornwall
summary: A teenage New Yorker with a flair for impulsive decisions, one of three friends who discover spider abilities as Madame Web guides them away from Ezekiel Sims.
source_notes: Comic counterpart becomes Spider-Woman (Julia Carpenter).

name: Kaecilius
summary: A former master of Kamar-Taj who betrayed the Ancient One to serve Dormammu, seeking eternal life. He was absorbed into the Dark Dimension.
source_notes: Primary antagonist of Doctor Strange (2016).

name: Karen Jenson
summary: A hematologist who is bitten by a vampire while treating Blade and helps him expose the vampire bloodfarming operation as Deacon Frost plots to summon the Blood God.
source_notes: Played by N'Bushe Wright in Blade (1998), the only heroine of the first film.

name: Karen Page
summary: An investigative journalist and law-firm clerk drawn into Matt Murdock's world. She uncovers the Fisk conspiracy and becomes a defiant reporter willing to burn for the truth.
source_notes: One of the trilogy's two love interests; comic counterpart dies by a shooter's bullet.

name: Katy Chen
debut_title: Shang-Chi and the Legend of the Ten Rings (2021)
summary: Shang-Chi's best friend and a valet-turned-archer who finds herself pulled into his family's war, proving a surprisingly gifted fighter.
source_notes: Shang-Chi's comic-relief best friend.
related_titles: Shang-Chi and the Legend of the Ten Rings (2021)

name: Kilgrave
summary: A sadistic man with the power to compel total obedience with a word. He enslaved Jessica, indelibly scarred her, and committed a wave of crimes before she finally strangled him to death.
source_notes: Primary antagonist of Jessica Jones season 1.

name: Kingo
summary: An Eternal who lived for centuries as a Bollywood star, able to fire cosmic energy projectiles. He declines to stop the Emergence but remains connected to his family.
source_notes: Comic-relief Eternal who wrestles with the moral choice.

name: Wilson Fisk
summary: A towering, implacable crime boss who had Matt Murdock and his father killed and rules Hell's Kitchen with brute force. He is confronted and nearly killed by Daredevil.
source_notes: Played by Michael Clarke Duncan in Daredevil (2003), a distinct variant from the Netflix Kingpin.

name: Korg
summary: A Kronan gladiator friend of Thor who leads the revolution against the Grandmaster, later runs the New Asgard tourism office and becomes a father figure.
source_notes: Writer/director Taika Waititi voices Korg.

name: Kraglin Obfonteri
summary: Yondu's loyal first mate who becomes one of the new Ravagers. He wields Yondu's whistling arrow after inheriting it and serves as a trusted lieutenant to the Guardians and the Ravager crew.
source_notes: Inherits Yondu's fin and arrow; helps lead the new Ravagers in Vol. 3.

name: Sergei Kravinoff
summary: A Russian aristocrat whose near-death encounter with a lion granted him enhanced strength and an animal connection. He hunts the villains who threaten his family, refusing to use guns against his prey.
source_notes: The SSU's anti-hero take on the classic Spider-Man villain.

name: Kro
summary: A shape-shifting, regenerating Deviant who hunts the Eternals and kills Ajak and Gilgamesh. He is destroyed by Sersi.
source_notes: Primary monster antagonist of Eternals (2021).

name: Lincoln Campbell
summary: An Inhuman with electrical powers who is torn between his Afterlife community and S.H.I.E.L.D. He sacrifices himself by piloting the Quinjet containing the Kree blob into space, destroying Hive's Inhuman conversion program.
source_notes: Recurring in Agents of S.H.I.E.L.D. seasons 2–3; Luke Mitchell also appeared in Blindspot.

name: Dr. Curt Connors
summary: A one-armed OsCorp geneticist who regrew his arm with a lizard-based serum but devolved into a monstrous, feral Lizard bent on 'rebuilding' humanity. He was cured, then pulled into No Way Home's multiversal breach.
source_notes: Appears in No Way Home as a variant.

name: Loki
summary: God of Mischief
source_notes: Confirmed for Avengers: Doomsday (cross-listed from the 30-member cast)

name: Luis
summary: Scott Lang's fast-talking former cellmate and partner-in-crime who provides rambling exposition and comic relief across the Ant-Man films.
source_notes: Known for his long-winded storytelling sequences.

name: Carl Lucas
summary: An ex-convict whose body was hardened by an experimental prison procedure, making him bulletproof and superhumanly strong. He protects Harlem as a hero-for-hire, married briefly to Jessica Jones, and eventually ran for office to save his neighbourhood.
source_notes: Debuts in Jessica Jones before headlining his own series.

name: Lylla
summary: A wise, kind otter and Rocket's closest companion from the High Evolutionary's experiments on Counter-Earth. She dreamed with Rocket of a free life among the stars, only to be gunned down before they could escape — the loss that still haunts Rocket.
source_notes: Her death in Vol. 3's flashbacks is presented as the emotional core of Rocket's arc.
notes: Memorial: Guardians' lab-animal friend. Killed by the High Evolutionary's forces.

name: Cassandra Webb
summary: A New York paramedic who begins seeing fragmented visions of the future after a near-fatal incident, learning to guide the young women who will become the Spider-Women against the hunter Ezekiel Sims.
source_notes: The SSU's clairvoyant hero; connects the Spider-Girls.

name: Erik Lehnsherr
summary: Master of magnetism
source_notes: Confirmed for Avengers: Doomsday (cross-listed from the 30-member cast)

name: Erik Lehnsherr
summary: A Holocaust survivor who controls magnetism and believes mutants must dominate rather than coexist. He oscillates between villain and ally of the X-Men across the Fox films.
source_notes: Played by Ian McKellen and Michael Fassbender at different ages; sees Xavier as his friend and rival.

name: Erik Lehnsherr (young)
summary: The younger Erik Lehnsherr of the prequel films, who finds an ally in Xavier before their philosophies diverge and he becomes Magneto.
source_notes: Michael Fassbender's young-timeline version tracked separately from Ian McKellen's.

name: Makkari
summary: An Eternal who moves and thinks at superhuman speeds, able to read any language. She is deaf and communicates in American Sign Language. She joins the fight to stop the Emergence.
source_notes: The MCU's first deaf superhero; a fan-favorite Eternal.

name: Malcolm Ducasse
summary: Jessica's recovering-addict neighbor who becomes her harried office assistant and eventually an independent investigative reporter.
source_notes: One of the few people Jessica genuinely trusts.

name: Malekith
summary: The leader of the Dark Elves who sought to plunge the universe back into darkness using the Reality Stone (the Aether). Killed and the Aether recovered by Sif and Volstagg, who deliver it to the Collector.
source_notes: Primary villain of The Dark World (2013); central to the Fakeville scene with Loki.

name: The Man-Thing
summary: A scientist transformed into a giant plant-monster guardian of a swamp, empowered by the Nexus of All Realities. He rises to defend the land from corporate corruption.
source_notes: Played by Conan Stevens in Man-Thing (2005), a direct-to-video film.

name: Mantis
summary: Raised by Ego as a sleeping servant with the power to sense and manipulate emotions. She uses that empathy to help stop Ego, joins the Guardians, and at the end of Vol. 3 leaves to discover her own path across the galaxy.
source_notes: Ego's daughter, making her Peter Quill's sister; departs the Guardians in Vol. 3.

name: Maria Hill
summary: Nick Fury's trusted deputy commander at S.H.I.E.L.D. who survived its collapse and worked with the Avengers. She was killed by a Skrull impersonating Fury in Secret Invasion (2023).
source_notes: Killed in Secret Invasion (2023).

name: Mariah Dillard
summary: A Harlem councilwoman who concealed her criminal empire behind a community-activist façade, killing family, cops and rivals to keep power. She was shot dead by her own daughter Tilda during a showdown.
source_notes: Rises from politician to crime boss across Luke Cage.

name: Matt Murdock
summary: A blind attorney who was blinded and superhumanly sensitized by radioactive waste. By day he defends the innocent; by night he hunts criminals as the horned vigilante Daredevil.
source_notes: Played by Ben Affleck in Daredevil (2003), a distinct variant from the Netflix Matt Murdock.

name: Matt Murdock
summary: A blind lawyer who fights crime at night with radar senses honed by a chemical accident that took his sight. He defends Hell's Kitchen as Daredevil, struggles with guilt and faith, and was pulled into the wider MCU with appearances in She-Hulk and Daredevil: Born Again.
source_notes: The same Charlie Cox incarnation continues in the MCU's Daredevil: Born Again (2025).

name: Mattie Franklin
summary: An outspoken, rebellious teenager and loyal friend, one of the three girls fated to become spider-powered heroes whose paths are guided by Madame Web away from Ezekiel Sims.
image_alt: Mattie Washburn House at 8660 Franklin Street, Windsor, California.  View looking northeast.
source_notes: Comics' Mattie Franklin was one of several Spider-Women.

name: M'Baku
summary: Leader of the Jabari
source_notes: Confirmed for Avengers: Doomsday (cross-listed from the 30-member cast)

name: Melinda May
summary: A legendary S.H.I.E.L.D. pilot and combat specialist haunted by the Bahrain incident. She is Coulson's most trusted operative, becomes Director of S.H.I.E.L.D. after the Chronicom war, and holds the team together through every crisis.
source_notes: Co-lead of Agents of S.H.I.E.L.D. seasons 1–7; Ming-Na Wen also played Mulan (1998) and Fen'ris Shao.

name: Mephistopheles
summary: The Devil himself, who engineers Johnny Blaze's transformation. He later wipes Johnny's memory before returning in Spirit of Vengeance to reclaim his son.
source_notes: Played by Peter Fonda in Ghost Rider (2007) and Ciarán Hinds in Spirit of Vengeance (2011).

name: Micro
summary: Howard Saint's ruthless lieutenant who carries out the massacre. He later betrays Saint to save his own life.
source_notes: Played by Wayne Knight in The Punisher (2004).

name: Microchip
summary: A criminal weapons-software expert blackmailed into working for Jigsaw. He is ultimately killed in the final confrontation.
source_notes: Played by Ewan Bremner in Punisher: War Zone (2008).

name: Miek
summary: A mute insectoid gladiator who becomes Korg's loyal companion and follows the New Asgardians through Ragnarok and the Battle of Earth.
source_notes: Only communicates through gestures.

name: Lucien Crown
summary: Michael Morbius's wealthy childhood friend who shared the same blood disease. After injecting himself with the same bat serum, he embraced his monstrous vampirism before being destroyed by Morbius.
source_notes: The antagonist of Morbius (2022).

name: Mercedes Knight
summary: A sharp Harlem detective who partners with Luke Cage, loses her arm to Diamondback, and is given a bionic prosthetic by Danny Rand to keep fighting as the city's sworn protector.
source_notes: Gained her bionic arm in The Defenders.

name: Mary Jane Watson
summary: Peter Parker's lifelong love, an aspiring actress who runs between superhero tragedy and her own ambitions. She finally married Peter before the multiversal breach.
source_notes: Peter's on-again, off-again partner across the Raimi trilogy.

name: Dr. Michael Morbius
summary: A brilliant Nobel-winning biologist with a rare blood disease who transformed himself with bat DNA, gaining vampiric powers and a thirst for blood. He wages war on his former friend Milo and the vampire he became.
source_notes: The Living Vampire of the SSU; frog-meme beloved in pop culture.

name: Karl Mordo
summary: A master sorcerer who rebelled against the ancient rules after the Ancient One's deception, declaring war on sorcerers who break the laws of nature.
source_notes: Turns antagonist in the post-credits scene of Doctor Strange (2016).

name: Raven Darkhölme
summary: The shape-shifting spy
source_notes: Confirmed for Avengers: Doomsday (cross-listed from the 30-member cast)

name: Raven Darkholme
summary: A blue-skinned shapeshifter raised as a sister to Charles Xavier who cycles between the X-Men and Magneto's Brotherhood, becoming a pivotal figure in the young-timeline films.
source_notes: Played by Rebecca Romijn in the original timeline and Jennifer Lawrence in the prequels.

name: Nakia
summary: A Wakandan spy and War Dog who once advocated for helping the outside world. She later helps Shuri reclaim the heart-shaped herb and leads an outreach team to help the wider world in Wakanda Forever.
source_notes: Lupita Nyong'o's character of the Wakandan War Dogs.

name: Namor
summary: King of Talokan
image_alt: Guillermo Namor Kong, membre de l'Assemblée constituante chilienne.
source_notes: Confirmed for Avengers: Doomsday (cross-listed from the 30-member cast)

name: Namora
summary: Warrior of Talokan
image_alt: portrait of Fernando Namora, portuguese writer (1919-1989)
source_notes: Confirmed for Avengers: Doomsday (cross-listed from the 30-member cast)

name: Nathaniel Malick
summary: Gideon Malick's younger brother who uses the Chronicom time-travel technology to rewrite HYDRA's history and build his own version of S.H.I.E.L.D. He kidnaps and converts young Inhumans to serve him, but is killed when the team's final timeline correction erases his altered history.
source_notes: Primary antagonist of Agents of S.H.I.E.L.D. season 7.

name: Nebula
summary: Thanos's cybernetically rebuilt daughter who endured torture each time she lost to Gamora. She turns against her father, helps the Avengers in the Time Heist, and eventually finds a home with the Ravagers before rebuilding them in Vol. 3.
source_notes: Tortured by Thanos repeatedly as a child; key to the Time Heist's Nebula/Gamora encounters in Endgame.

name: Nick Fury
summary: Eyepatch-wearing spymaster who assembled the Avengers Initiative. Director of S.H.I.E.L.D., architect of the team, later operating inside S.A.B.E.R. in space.
source_notes: Post-credits debut in Iron Man (2008) proposing the Avengers Initiative.

name: Nick Fury
summary: The commander of S.H.I.E.L.D. in a television film continuity. He faces off against the terrorist organization HYDRA, led by Baron Strucker, who plots to release a deadly bio-weapon over Manhattan.
image_alt: Screen capture from Nick Fury: Agent of S.H.I.E.L.D. (1998).Featuring David Hasselhoff as Nick Fury.
source_notes: Played by David Hasselhoff in the 1998 television film, a distinct variant from Samuel L. Jackson's MCU Nick Fury.

name: Kurt Wagner
summary: The blue teleporter
source_notes: Confirmed for Avengers: Doomsday (cross-listed from the 30-member cast)

name: Kurt Wagner
summary: A deeply devout, blue-furred mutant who can teleport short distances, leaving a puff of smoke and brimstone scent. A beloved member of the X-Men in both eras.
image_alt: wagner Before and After 1 makeover plastic surgery
source_notes: Played by Alan Cumming and Kodi Smit-McPhee.

name: Nobu Yoshioka
summary: A senior Hand lieutenant and nimble swordsman who repeatedly battles Daredevil, dying and being revived through the Hand's resurrection rite until Matt finally burns his body to keep him down.
source_notes: Electra's killer; burned for good in Daredevil season 2.

name: Nomak
summary: A pureblood vampire deformed into a ravenous 'Reaper' by a flawed blood-splicing experiment. He leads the Reapers in a war against both vampire houses and the Daywalker.
source_notes: Primary antagonist of Blade II (2002).

name: Will Simpson
summary: A black-ops soldier with a skull-like face and a red-pill-fuelled rage, an ex-boyfriend of Trish who hunted Jessica on orders before his dependence on the pill drove him to a fatal crash.
source_notes: The series' take on the comics' war-lunatic Nuke.

name: Odin
summary: The Allfather of Asgard and father of Thor, Hela and Loki. He conquered the Nine Realms in his youth and later banished Thor to teach him humility, dying in Thor: Ragnarok with the truth about Hela left to his sons.
image_alt: Promotional image of Anthony Hopkins as Odin in the Marvel Studios film, Thor.
source_notes: Dies peacefully in Ragnarok (2017), revealing Hela's existence to Thor.

name: Okoye
summary: The general of the Dora Milaje and a formidable spear-fighter. She has served Wakanda's throne across the Black Panther films and the Avengers' final battle, later leading Wakanda's forces in Wakanda Forever.
image_alt: Dr Ngozi Franca Okoye, Nigerian Biochemist, Professor(Associate)
source_notes: One of Wakanda's most prominent warriors in Black Panther films and Endgame.

name: Peggy Carter
summary: A founder of S.H.I.E.L.D. and the love of Steve Rogers's life. She co-founded the agency after World War II, was reunited with Steve in the 1970s timeline, and the 2019-era Steve chose to live out his life with her in the past.
image_alt: Promotional image of Hayley Atwell as Peggy Carter in the Marvel Studios film, Captain America: The First Avenger.
source_notes: Co-founded S.H.I.E.L.D.; Steve Rogers retires to a branch where she exists and they marry.

name: Pete Kasady
summary: A corrupt land developer determined to seize the swamp's oil at any cost. Intoxicated by the Nexus's power, he is dragged to his death by the Man-Thing.
source_notes: Played by Matthew Le Nevez in Man-Thing (2005).

name: Phastos
summary: An Eternal who invented technology for humanity over millennia, living quietly with his husband and son. He recommits to protecting Earth at the film's end.
source_notes: The MCU's first gay married superhero family.

name: Phil Coulson
summary: A calm, loyal S.H.I.E.L.D. agent who assembled the Avengers and was killed by Loki in The Avengers, later revived by Project T.A.H.I.T.I. to lead the agents of S.H.I.E.L.D. for many seasons.
source_notes: Returned to the main films' canon through a variant in Captain Marvel (2019) and Legacy contexts; leads the Agents of S.H.I.E.L.D. series.

name: Phil Coulson
summary: S.H.I.E.L.D. agent resurrected after the Battle of New York using Tahiti protocol and Kree blood. He leads the S.H.I.E.L.D. team through HYDRA's fall, the Inhuman outbreak, the Framework, and the time-traveling Chronicom war, ultimately disappearing during the final mission.
source_notes: Main protagonist of Agents of S.H.I.E.L.D. seasons 1–5; played by Clark Gregg. The MCU film character dies in The Avengers; this AOS variant was secretly resurrected.

name: Piper
summary: A loyal S.H.I.E.L.D. agent who serves under May and Mack. She pilots the Zephyr One during the Chronicom war and proves herself under pressure repeatedly.
source_notes: Recurring in Agents of S.H.I.E.L.D. seasons 3–7.

name: Charles Xavier (young)
summary: The younger incarnation of Charles Xavier seen in the prequel films, who founds the X-Men and struggles with his wheelchair-bound fate and his bond with Magneto.
source_notes: James McAvoy's version is tracked separately from Patrick Stewart's as a distinct young-timeline variant.

name: Charles Xavier
summary: Founder of the X-Men
source_notes: Confirmed for Avengers: Doomsday (cross-listed from the 30-member cast)
related_titles: Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness (2022)

name: Pietro Maximoff
summary: A superfast mutant with a wisecracking streak whose famous slow-motion rescue sequences defined the young-timeline films. A variant of him appears in the MCU series WandaVision.
source_notes: Played by Evan Peters; distinct from the MCU's own Pietro also played by Aaron Taylor-Johnson.

name: Raina
summary: A former journalist turned Centipede Group operative who desperately wants to undergo Terrigenesis. After transforming into an Inhuman with precognitive flower-touch abilities, she is killed when her visions show a devastating future, driving her to suicide.
image_alt: Suresh Raina grace the 'Salaam Sachin' conclave
source_notes: Recurring antagonist in Agents of S.H.I.E.L.D. seasons 1–2; Ruth Negga later starred in Prey (2022) and voiced a character in What If...?

name: Ramonda
summary: The mother of T'Challa and Shuri and the matriarch of Wakanda's royal family. She assumed the throne after her son's death and drowned while rescuing Riri Williams from Namor's forces in Wakanda Forever.
source_notes: A triumphant Angela Bassett portrayal; dies in Wakanda Forever.

name: Alexei Shostakov
summary: The Red Guardian
image_alt: Florence Pugh & David Harbour in an interview with Escorpión Dorado in 2025  (2:00)
source_notes: Confirmed for Avengers: Doomsday (cross-listed from the 30-member cast)

name: Johann Schmidt
summary: Captain America's monstrous Nazi enemy with a red, disfigured face. He reveals he is Steve Rogers' lifelong friend aligned with fascism and is defeated in a final confrontation.
image_alt: Martin Johann Schmidt (Kremser-Schmidt) (around 1790) by Paul Haubenstricker
source_notes: Played by Scott Paulin in Captain America (1990), a distinct variant from Hugo Weaving's MCU Red Skull.

name: Reed Richards
summary: Leader of the Fantastic Four
source_notes: Confirmed for Avengers: Doomsday (cross-listed from the 30-member cast)

name: Reed Richards
summary: A brilliant scientist who gains the ability to stretch his body to incredible lengths and shapes. He leads the Fantastic Four and is the team's strategic genius.
source_notes: Played by Ioan Gruffudd (2005) and Miles Teller (2015).
related_titles: Fantastic Four: Rise of the Silver Surfer (2007)

name: Nikolai Kravinoff
summary: Sergei's ambitious half-brother who experiments on himself with a rhinoceros serum, transforming into a monstrous human-rhino hybrid hunting his brother for control of the family empire.
source_notes: A separate, animal-berserker Rhino from the Webb-universe version.

name: Aleksei Sytsevich
summary: A Russian gangster who dons a towering mechanized rhino suit. He rampaged through Manhattan in the film's cliffhanger ending, brawling with Spider-Man as sirens blared.
source_notes: Final battle set-up that was never followed up due to the franchise's reboot.

name: Aleksei Ribery
summary: Kraven's ruthless father, a powerful crime lord who hunted exotic animals for sport and sought to expand his empire, ultimately meeting his end at the hands of his own sons.
source_notes: The villainous family patriarch of Kraven the Hunter.

name: Riri Williams
summary: A teenage M.I.T. engineering prodigy who builds a powered suit. Captured by Namor as leverage, she is rescued by Shuri and later starred in the Ironheart series.
source_notes: Featured in Ironheart (Disney+); debut in Wakanda Forever.

name: Robert Gonzalez
summary: A veteran S.H.I.E.L.D. officer who leads the 'Real S.H.I.E.L.D.' faction opposed to Coulson's leadership. He is principled but authoritarian and is killed during the Inhuman crisis on the Iliad.
image_alt: Picture of a detail from Félix González-Torres's artwork "Untitled" (Portrait of Robert Vifian) (1993) at the National Portrait Gallery in Washington, D.C., in 2025, as part of the exhibition Felix Gonzalez-Torres: Always To Return. The phrase "First T.V. 1966" is painted in silver italic font on a wall near the ceiling, just below the decorative molding at the top of the wall. The phrase is one part of a larger date portrait made by the artist and modified by the curators. This phrase was included in the first iteration of the work created by the artist.
source_notes: Recurring in Agents of S.H.I.E.L.D. season 2; Edward James Olmos brings significant gravitas to the role.

name: Rocket
summary: A genetically engineered raccoon-like weapons expert created by the High Evolutionary. He becomes the new leader of the Guardians after Adam Warlock nearly kills him, then takes a captain's chair as the team reboots in Vol. 3.
source_notes: Origin revealed fully in Vol. 3; becomes the Guardians' captain at its end.

name: Marie D'Ancanto
summary: A mutant who absorbs the powers, memories, and life-force of anyone she touches skin-to-skin, making human contact dangerous. She is a central early X-Men member.
source_notes: Played by Anna Paquin in the original trilogy.

name: Ronan
summary: A fanatical Kree zealot who sought to destroy Xandar and, later, all of planet Xandar's enemies. Betrayed by his allies and destroyed by the Guardians after wielding one Infinity Stone too many.
source_notes: First appears (briefly) in Captain Marvel (2019) set in 1995.

name: Victor Creed
summary: A feral, fanged mutant who shares Wolverine's healing factor and animal instincts, and serves as his lifelong rival. He appears in the first X-Men film and Wolverine's origin story.
source_notes: Played by Tyler Mane (X-Men 2000) and Liev Schreiber (X-Men Origins: Wolverine 2009).

name: Sam Wilson
summary: The new Captain America
source_notes: Confirmed for Avengers: Doomsday (cross-listed from the 30-member cast)
related_titles: The Falcon and the Winter Soldier (2021)

name: Flint Marko
summary: A desperate fugitive transformed into living sand by a particle accelerator. He was revealed to be the true killer of Uncle Ben, but chose redemption alongside Spider-Man against Venom.
source_notes: Tragic figure who accidentally killed Uncle Ben; turns ally against Venom.

name: Wanda Maximoff
summary: Sokovian chaos-magic user who evolved from Ultron's weapon into the Scarlet Witch. Multi-Doctor Strange antagonist who destroyed Kamar-Taj and died under Mount Wundagore.
source_notes: Exact fate after the Wundagore collapse was unconfirmed at snapshot; treated as Deceased per Multiverse of Madness events.
related_titles: Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness (2022)

name: Scott Lang
summary: The size-shifting Avenger

About Ant-Man
The next evolution of the Marvel Cinematic Universe brings a founding member of The Avengers to the big screen for the first time with Marvel Studios’ “Ant-Man.” Armed with the astonishing ability to shrink in scale but increase in strength, master thief Scott Lang must embrace his inner-hero and help his mentor, Dr. Hank Pym, protect the secret behind his spectacular Ant-Man suit from a new generation of towering threats. Against seemingly insurmountable obstacles, Pym and Lang must plan and pull off a heist that will save the world. 
Marvel’s “Ant-Man” stars Paul Rudd as Scott Lang aka Ant-Man, Evangeline Lilly as Hope Van Dyne, Corey Stoll as Darren Cross aka Yellowjacket, Bobby Cannavale as Paxton, Michael Peña as Luis, Judy Greer as Maggie, Tip “Ti” Harris as Dave, David Dastmalchian as Kurt, Wood Harris as Gale, Jordi Mollà as Castillo and Michael Douglas as Hank Pym.

name: Sersi
summary: An Eternal with the power to transmute matter, who chose to live among humans. She reunites the Eternals to stop the Emergence and becomes their de facto leader, leaving Earth with them at the film's end.
source_notes: Primary protagonist of Eternals (2021).

name: Hernán Alvarez
summary: A slick enforcer and lieutenant who served Cottonmouth, then Maria, and closeted a partnership with Bushmaster. His calculating ambition ended with his death in the dust of Harlem's Paradise.
source_notes: A recurring villain across both Luke Cage seasons.

name: Xu Shang-Chi

summary: Master of the Ten Rings
source_notes: Confirmed for Avengers: Doomsday (cross-listed from the 30-member cast)
