name: Frances Barrison
summary: A pyrokinetic prisoner with a sonic scream who becomes Cletus Kasady's love interest and ally, unleashing chaos while Carnage battles Venom.
source_notes: Pairs with Carnage in Let There Be Carnage.

name: Shuri
summary: The Black Panther
source_notes: Confirmed for Avengers: Doomsday (cross-listed from the 30-member cast)

name: Sif
summary: A fierce Asgardian warrior and close friend of Thor who fights beside the Warriors Three. She leads an Asgardian squad on a mission to free a Kree refugee settlement in Loki, season 2.
image_alt: Promotional image of Jaimie Alexander as Sif in the Marvel Studios film, Thor.
source_notes: Appears across the Thor films and Loki (2021/2023).

name: Norrin Radd
debut_title: Fantastic Four: Rise of the Silver Surfer (2007)
summary: A cosmic herald bonded to a silver surfboard who scouts worlds for Galactus. He rebels against his master after connecting with humanity in Rise of the Silver Surfer.
source_notes: Portrayed by Doug Jones (physical) and voiced by Laurence Fishburne in Rise of the Silver Surfer (2007).
related_titles: Fantastic Four: Rise of the Silver Surfer (2007)

name: Skurge
summary: An Asgardian warrior who serves Hela as her Executioner after she conquers Asgard, but redeems himself in the final battle, holding the Bifrost bridge against her undead army.
source_notes: Dies holding the bridge in Ragnarok.

name: Sonny Burch
summary: A black-market dealer who tried to seize Pym's shrinking tech in Ant-Man and the Wasp. He was left stranded on a beach after a deal went sideways.
source_notes: Left in a humorous cliffhanger at the end of Ant-Man and the Wasp.

name: Peter Parker
summary: The quip-heavy, skateboarding Peter Parker of the Webb duology, orphaned and seeking the truth about his parents. He lost Gwen Stacy and blamed himself, then redeemed himself by saving Michelle in No Way Home.
source_notes: Returns for redemption arc in Spider-Man: No Way Home (2021).

name: Peter Parker
summary: The shy, noble Peter Parker bitten by a genetically-enhanced spider in the Raimi trilogy. He fought the Green Goblin, Doctor Octopus and Venom, and crossed into the MCU during the multiversal breach of No Way Home, where he reunited with his alternate-universe counterparts.
source_notes: The first big-screen Spider-Man; returns as a variant in Spider-Man: No Way Home (2021).

name: Sprite
summary: An Eternal who appears forever young, able to project illusions. Bitter about never growing up, she sided with Ikaris before being reborn as a mortal human.
source_notes: Reborn mortal using a fragment of the Uni-Mind in Eternals (2021).

name: Peter Quill
summary: Half-human, half-Celestial abducted from Earth in 1988 and raised by the Ravager Yondu. Leader of the Guardians, he sacrificed his father Ego's power to save the galaxy. Blipped for five years after the Snap, then rejoined his found family before the Guardians' departure with a new team.
source_notes: Key player across both Guardians films, the two Avengers films, and the Guardians Holiday Special; leaves with the new Guardians at the end of Vol. 3.

name: Stick
summary: The grizzled blind martial artist who trained young Matt Murdock to master his senses, and the leader of the Chaste in their ancient war against the Hand. He was beheaded by the resurrected Elektra.
image_alt: Fawn and white Welsh Corgi puppy, standing on rear legs and sticking out the tongue.
source_notes: Daredevil's mentor; slays members of the Hand.

name: Stick
summary: A blind martial-arts master and leader of the warrior order the Chaste. In the spinoff film he recruits Elektra to defeat the Hand's assassins.
source_notes: Played by Terence Stamp in Elektra (2005), a distinct variant from the Netflix Stick.

name: Ororo Munroe
summary: A mutant able to control the weather, and one of the X-Men's most formidable core members across both the original and young-timeline teams.
source_notes: Played by Halle Berry and Alexandra Shipp.

name: Sue Storm
summary: The Invisible Woman
source_notes: Confirmed for Avengers: Doomsday (cross-listed from the 30-member cast)

name: Susan Storm
summary: A scientist who can turn invisible and project protective force fields. She is Reed's partner and the team's emotional anchor.
source_notes: Played by Jessica Alba (2005) and Kate Mara (2015).
related_titles: Fantastic Four: Rise of the Silver Surfer (2007)

name: Talos
summary: A Skrull general who once led his people against the Kree, Talos became an ally of Carol Danvers and later worked with Nick Fury, living disguised among humans on Earth. He was killed in Secret Invasion while trying to find his captured daughter.
source_notes: Killed by Gravik in Secret Invasion; his daughter G'iah survives.

name: Taserface
summary: A mutinous Ravager who staged a coup against Yondu after the failed Ego job. He reveals the Ravagers' code that condemns Yondu's clan, and is later killed.
source_notes: A comic-relief villain from Vol. 2.

name: T'Challa
summary: King of Wakanda and the Black Panther who defended his nation and joined the fight against Thanos. He sacrificed himself to save Okoye and Wanda during the Outriders' assault, but was restored by the Blip reversal before his death in Wakanda Forever.
source_notes: Killed in the Snap's aftermath in Infinity War; restored in Endgame; the MCU character dies before Wakanda Forever (2022), reflecting the passing of Chadwick Boseman.

name: Teefs
summary: A gentle walrus and one of Rocket's fellow experiment subjects in the High Evolutionary's lab. Slow-moving but sweet, he was killed along with Lylla and Floor on their failed escape.
source_notes: Featured in Vol. 3 flashbacks; killed in the same scene as Lylla.

name: The Overlord
summary: A malevolent interdimensional entity that manifests by possessing a human body to open a doorway through which its power can enter Earth. It is destroyed by Howard and Beverly.
source_notes: Played by Jeffrey Jones in Howard the Duck (1986).

name: Thena
summary: A warrior Eternal who crafts weapons from cosmic energy and suffers from a degenerative battle-madness called Mahd Wy'ry. She joins the fight to stop the Emergence.
source_notes: Gilgamesh's close companion among the Eternals.

name: Thor
summary: The God of Thunder
image_alt: A still from the 2013 film Thor: The Dark World showing actor Chris Hemsworth as Thor
source_notes: Confirmed for Avengers: Doomsday (cross-listed from the 30-member cast)

name: Trish Walker
summary: Jessica's childhood best friend and a former child-star turned radio host. Desperate to be a hero, she trains brutally, gains powers through the experimental compound, takes the name Hellcat, and is ultimately imprisoned for revenge killings.
source_notes: Becomes Hellcat in Jessica Jones season 3.

name: Typhoid Mary
summary: A deadly Hand assassin who can create illusions and wield a lethal touch. She is sent to kill the girl Elektra protects and is ultimately defeated.
image_alt: Typhoid Mary in typhoid ward of New York city
source_notes: Played by Natassia Malthe in Elektra (2005).

name: Ulysses Klaue
summary: A black-market arms dealer who trafficked Vibranium and crossed Ultron in Age of Ultron. He aided Killmonger's plot against Wakanda before Killmonger shot him.
source_notes: Killed by Killmonger in Black Panther (2018).

name: Ben Parker
summary: Peter's gentle uncle whose murder imparted the lesson that 'with great power there must also come great responsibility.' He was shot by the fleeing Flint Marko.
image_alt: 04/01/11 Cardiff V Leeds, Championship, Cardiff City Stadium, Cardiff, Wales
source_notes: His death motivates Peter to become Spider-Man.

name: Brunnhilde
summary: The last of the legendary Valkyries, a hard-drinking scavenger who survives Hela's purge. She helps Thor defeat Hela, fights the Black Order at the Battle of Earth, and is crowned the new King of New Asgard.
source_notes: King of New Asgard from the end of Endgame onward.

name: Eddie Brock
summary: A freelance investigative journalist who bonded with an alien symbiote named Venom, becoming a violent anti-hero 'lethal protector' of San Francisco. A variant of him was briefly pulled into the MCU and left a piece of the symbiote behind.
source_notes: Eddie and the Venom symbiote share one body; a variant appears in No Way Home's mid-credits scene.

name: Venom
summary: The chaotic, hungry alien symbiote bonded to Eddie Brock. It speaks its own thoughts, feeds on chocolates and host brains, and left a fragment in the MCU when a variant was pulled through at the end of No Way Home.
source_notes: A surviving droplet of the symbiote remains in the MCU.

name: Vision
summary: Sentient android built from Ultron's shell and J.A.R.V.I.S., bonded to the Mind Stone. Killed by Thanos in 2018, later rebuilt as White Vision in Westview.
source_notes: Status reflects the rebuilt White Vision departing Westview in WandaVision; whereabouts unconfirmed at snapshot.

name: Volstagg
summary: A jovial, enormous Asgardian warrior of the Warriors Three, killed by Hela in Thor: Ragnarok.
source_notes: Killed by Hela in Ragnarok (2017); actor Ray Stevenson passed away in 2023.

name: James Rhodes
summary: U.S. Air Force liaison who wore Tony Stark's armor as War Machine, later fielding his own heavy-arsenal suit alongside the Avengers.
source_notes: First portrayed by Terrence Howard in Iron Man (2008), then Don Cheadle from Iron Man 2 onward.

name: Xu Wenwu
debut_title: Shang-Chi and the Legend of the Ten Rings (2021)
summary: The immortal warlord who wielded the Ten Rings for a thousand years and fathered Shang-Chi. Nagged by grief for his wife, he was slain by the Dweller-in-Darkness, which then possessed him.
source_notes: The Mandarin reveal in Shang-Chi; killed by the Dweller-in-Darkness.
related_titles: Shang-Chi and the Legend of the Ten Rings (2021)

name: Wilson Fisk
summary: A physically massive, ruthless crime lord who despises his own monstrosity and wants to rebuild Hell's Kitchen in his image. He fights Daredevil, escapes prison, and rises as New York's mayoral kingpin in the MCU's Echo and Daredevil: Born Again.
source_notes: The same Vincent D'Onofrio incarnation appears in Hawkeye (2021) and Echo (2024).

name: Logan
summary: A near-immortal mutant with retractable adamantium claws and a healing factor, and the breakout star of the Fox X-Men films. He died in Logan (2017) but returned in Deadpool & Wolverine (2024) across variant timelines.
source_notes: Played by Hugh Jackman for over two decades; death in Logan (2017); returns as variants in Deadpool & Wolverine (2024).

name: Wong
summary: The keeper of the Kamar-Taj library who becomes the MCU's Sorcerer Supreme and an occasional Avenger. He loses the multiversal suite of the Darkhold in Multiverse of Madness.
source_notes: Librarian of Kamar-Taj; promoted to Sorcerer Supreme.
related_titles: Shang-Chi and the Legend of the Ten Rings (2021)
Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness (2022)

name: Laura Kinney
summary: A young clone of Wolverine created as a weapon, inheriting his adamantium claws and healing factor. She is the emotional heart of Logan and carries on his legacy.
source_notes: Played by Dafne Keen in Logan (2017).

name: Xu Xialing
debut_title: Shang-Chi and the Legend of the Ten Rings (2021)
summary: Shang-Chi's estranged younger sister who secretly runs a criminal underground. She reunites with her brother against their father and later reforms the Ten Rings organization.
source_notes: Featured in Shang-Chi; associated with the Ten Rings post-film.
related_titles: Shang-Chi and the Legend of the Ten Rings (2021)

name: Yelena Belova
summary: The second Black Widow
source_notes: Confirmed for Avengers: Doomsday (cross-listed from the 30-member cast)

name: Elena Rodriguez
summary: A Colombian Inhuman who can accelerate to super-speed and bounce back to her starting point like a yo-yo. She joins the Secret Warriors, loses her forearms during the Chronicom war, and receives prosthetic replacements from Fitz.
source_notes: Recurring seasons 3–5; regular season 6–7 of Agents of S.H.I.E.L.D. Also starred in the Slingshot digital series.

name: Yondu Udonta
summary: The blue-skinned Ravager who abducted Peter Quill and raised him despite a fatherly bond he hid behind gruffness. He sacrifices himself to save Peter in the vacuum of space in Vol. 2 and dies a hero's death honored by the Ravager fleet.
source_notes: The 2014 Yondu who attacks the Guardians in the first film is the same character who later redeems himself and dies in Vol. 2.
